FACT_ID: SEC09-C01 | anchor: A49
Statement: Flex-lane usability is shown by overhead indications with green arrow meaning use allowed and red X meaning use prohibited.
Explanation: Reversible lanes change by time of day; driver must check indication before entering.
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: SEC09-C02 | anchor: A49B
Statement: Freeway operation requires two-second minimum following gap, no U-turns, no emergency-lane driving, and left-lane move-over when approached from behind.
Explanation: Higher speeds demand longer gap; impeding left-lane traffic can draw a citation.
Source: [A49B -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: SEC09-C03 | anchor: A50
Statement: I-15 express lanes allow qualifying high-occupancy and decal traffic free and single-occupant traffic only with active express pass; crossing double white line is prohibited except at dotted access points.
Explanation: Access points are intermittent; handbook advises exiting one interchange early to reach desired exit.
Source: [A50 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: SEC09-C04 | anchor: A51
Statement: Ramp meters admit generally one vehicle per green and apply only when meter-on sign is lit; runaway ramps must not be used except in emergency.
Explanation: Meters regulate merge flow during heavy entry volumes; runaway ramps are reserved for brake-failure stops.
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: SEC09-C05 | anchor: A53
Statement: Yellow markings separate opposing directions and white markings separate same-direction flow with double-white express separation not to be crossed.
Explanation: Dashed side permits passing when on your side; solid controls prohibit movement across.
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: SEC09-C06 | anchor: A54
Statement: Shared center left-turn lane entry is limited to no more than 500 feet before the turn and requires mirror blind-spot and signal checks.
Explanation: Early entry creates head-on risk; limit keeps lane available for opposing turners.
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: SEC09-C07 | anchor: A54B
Statement: Utah basic speed law bars driving faster than reasonable and prudent, with handbook-listed defaults of 20 near schools, 25 business-residential, 55 major highways, and 65 to 80 on rural interstates as posted.
Explanation: Adverse weather narrow roads hills curves intersections work zones and emergency lights all require slowing; too-slow impeding can also be cited.
Source: [A54B -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: SEC09-C08 | anchor: A55
Statement: Roundabout approach requires slowing, yielding to circulating traffic and pedestrians, then proceeding to desired exit.
Explanation: Entry yields; no stop required when clear.
Source: [A55 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: SEC09-C09 | anchor: A56
Statement: Signal meanings include steady green go when clear, steady yellow about to turn red, flashing yellow proceed with caution, flashing yellow arrow turn after yielding, steady red stop, flashing red stop then proceed when clear, and red arrows stop and remain stopped for that movement.
Explanation: Left turns may show protected arrow, solid green, or flashing yellow arrow; one-way to one-way stranded left exception is narrowly described.
Source: [A56 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: SEC09-C10 | anchor: A60
Statement: Right-of-way is never assumed; yield to intersection occupant ahead, oncoming traffic on left turn, right-hand driver at simultaneous four-way stop, public-road traffic when entering from driveway, freeway traffic when merging, and any pedestrians or bicyclists still in intersection.
Explanation: Courtesy and defensive yielding override claimed priority; officer direction overrides signals.
Source: [A60 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0060]

High-yield: signals and ROW first, then markings, then freeway behavior, then speed law, then special interchanges.
Misconceptions: green means protected; right-on-red always allowed; crossing double white to exit express lane; stopping on tracks; U-turn on freeway; SPUI outage treated as four-way stop.
Mnemonics: RYG top-to-bottom; X means no; Dotted means door; 2-second space; 500-foot center lane.
